previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mrs. ___ was admitted for nausea, vomiting, and transient low-grade fever. Workup including CT scans of the head, abdomen, and pelvis, as well as cardiac enzymes, showed no acute pathology. Her symptoms were attributed to viral gastroenteritis, and she was treated with IV fluids and Zofran with good response. A mildly abnormal urinalysis prompted a course of ciprofloxacin despite negative cultures. Her chronic conditions—including hypertension, neuropathic chest pain, rheumatoid arthritis, and narcotic-treated pain—were managed with her baseline medications. She improved clinically, tolerated oral intake, and was discharged home with follow-up arranged. Her narcotic contract was continued, and she was advised to maintain laxative use.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ woman with shortness of breath.  Evaluate for
pneumonia.

COMPARISON:  Multiple priors, most recent CT chest without contrast ___ chest PA and lateral ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Portable AP chest x-ray.

FINDINGS:  The cardiac silhouette appears normal in size and unchanged from
___.  There is a rightward shift of the mediastinum with
elevated right hemidiaphragm, consistent with right lung volume loss. 
Surgical material is noted within the right hilus, consistent with remote
right upper lobectomy.  The pulmonary vasculature appears unremarkable.  The
bilateral lungs appear well aerated, with no evidence of consolidation or
pleural effusion.

The visualized osseous structures show no evidence of gross skeletal
abnormalities.

IMPRESSION:  No acute cardiopulmonary process.
